source:
I want to build a 3D racing game where the player controls a dragon flying through a sequence of rings to complete a course.

Here are the core requirements for the game:
1. Player Controller:
 • The player controls a 3D dragon character.
 • Flight controls should include pitch (up/down), yaw (left/right), and roll.
 • Include a forward thrust/speed mechanic, and gravity that pulls the dragon down slightly if they aren't actively flying.
2. Camera System:
 • Implement a third-person follow camera that stays behind and slightly above the dragon, smoothly rotating as the dragon turns.
3. Course & Ring Mechanics:
 • Create a system for placing floating rings in the environment.
 • The player must fly through the rings in a specific, numbered order.
 • When the player passes through the correct active ring, play a sound, change the ring's color (e.g., from yellow to green), and activate the next ring in the sequence.
4. Win/Loss State & UI:
 • Include a simple HUD (Heads Up Display) showing a countdown timer and a ring counter (e.g., "Rings: 3/10").
 • Win State: Passing through the final ring before time runs out.
 • Loss State: The timer hitting zero before the course is finished, or crashing into the ground/terrain.

image_prompt.text: The ground and terrain below the course, lethal on contact - crashing into it ends the run
The final ring of the sequence, where passing through ends the course
An open sky volume above varied terrain, flown through rather than walked across
floating rings placed at varying heights and distances along an aerial course

layout_placement.text: Detection at the last ring that ends the race if the timer has not expired
A recovery point restoring a crashed flyer with position, orientation and zeroed velocity
the rings must be passed in a specific numbered order, each one activating the next

notes: Preset caveat: Obstacle Race contributes a course recovery point, but the prompt makes crashing a loss state rather than a setback - kept in the handoff and flagged as rejected.
The numbered ring sequence is the whole course and no Racing option covers ordered pass-through gates, so it is carried as free text in both streams.
P6 was taken from the genre route, but there is no ground track to validate here - the route to keep coherent is a line through open air.
The dragon hints at a fantasy look, but the prompt never states a theme.

open_questions.ask: No theme was stated - should the world below read as high fantasy, or something else?
How many rings should the course have? The HUD example implies ten.

coverage_missing.ask: What should the world below the course look like?
How many rings, and how long is the timer?

answers.answer: Use 10 rings, as implied by the HUD example.
